obligation: Title IV breach report to FSA
citation: SAIG Enrollment Agreement (per DCL GEN-15-18); FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake
trigger: Actual or suspected breach of student information, or compromise of the college's SAIG or Department system access
deadline: Immediately upon an actual or suspected breach; do not wait for forensic confirmation; update as facts develop
notify: FSA (Cybersecurity Breach Intake Form and CPSSAIG@ed.gov)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Title IV participant with a SAIG Enrollment Agreement
notifying_entity: Cris Santos College (executive director of financial aid with the College CISO)
clock_starts: Suspicion, which here is the day the SOC tells the college (Day 0)

obligation: FTC notification event (Safeguards Rule)
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information involving at least 500 consumers; unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the ftc.gov form, with the content listed in 314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 380,000 consumers in the scenario
notifying_entity: Cris Santos College (College CISO as Qualified Individual, with counsel)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known to any employee, officer, or other agent; counsel treats Education Software staff operating the tenant as agents, so Day 0 at the latest

obligation: FTC notice: law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still due within 30 days of discovery and must include the determination; law enforcement may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 more days on written request
notify: FTC (inside the notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if law enforcement asks

obligation: FERPA record of the unauthorized disclosure
trigger: PII from education records disclosed without authorization
deadline: Record in each affected student's disclosure record, kept as long as the education record is kept; FERPA itself has no breach notification requirement
notify: Internal: the registrar records the incident and the parties if known; students may inspect the record
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - college students; each contracting college decides for its own records
notifying_entity: Cris Santos College (university registrar); each affected institution for its own records
clock_starts: When the affected students are identified

obligation: Qualified Individual report to the college board of trustees
trigger: Any security event
deadline: In the next annual written report (October); the board chair and the college president are briefed the same day under POL-03
notify: College board of trustees
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: State breach notification laws (generic)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents; definitions, encryption safe harbors, and regulator notice duties vary
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or other regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - online students live in all 50 states; apply each state where affected individuals reside
notifying_entity: Each division that owns the data (the college; Student Health for PHI and clinic records; customers for their own data)
clock_starts: Per state law; plan from the earliest determination date

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (name with SSN, financial account with access code, medical or health insurance information, and other listed elements; encrypted data excluded unless the key was taken)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)) for this individual notice only
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email; content per 501.171(4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 140,000 Florida college students and 2,100 Florida Student Health patients in the scenario
notifying_entity: Cris Santos College; Student Health (it may instead rely on its HIPAA notice under the federal-regulator path, with a copy to the Department)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs; content per 501.171(3)(b), including a copy of the individual notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Intercompany notice from Education Software to the college
trigger: An incident affecting the college tenant on the Campus Platform
deadline: Within 24 hours (group policy); the 2021 agreement sets no time
notify: College CISO and university registrar
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - policy now; contract term pending

obligation: Education Software notice to affected college customers
trigger: Incident affecting a customer tenant on the Campus Platform
deadline: Within 72 hours under the standard contract; shorter where negotiated
notify: Each affected customer's security contact; customers then make their own FSA, FTC, and state determinations
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 14 college customers in the scenario
notifying_entity: Education Software (support director with privacy counsel)

obligation: Education Software notice to affected districts
citation: District contracts; state student data privacy laws (generic)
trigger: Incident affecting a district tenant on the District Platform, including children's data
deadline: Within 72 hours under the standard contract; about 1,300 districts have state-specific terms (register due 2026-12-15, POAM-024)
notify: Each affected district's designated contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 3 districts in 2 states in the scenario

obligation: Third-party agent notice to a covered entity (Florida worked example)
trigger: A third-party agent that maintains personal information for a covered entity has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days after determining the breach or reason to believe one occurred
notify: The covered entity for which the data is maintained
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Education Software for Florida customers; Student Health for contracting colleges; the college's own vendors to the college

obligation: COPPA Rule: no breach notice provision
citation: 16 CFR Part 312 (312.8 security program; no breach notice section)
trigger: Incident affecting children's personal information
deadline: No regulatory notice clock; after the incident, evaluate and modify the program (312.8(b)(5)); FTC Act Section 5 exposure if safeguards were unreasonable
notify: None under the Rule; districts and families are told under contracts and state law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 17,000 children under 13 in the scenario

obligation: Customer institutions' own duties
citation: 16 CFR 314.4(j); SAIG Enrollment Agreement; 34 CFR 99.32; state law (customer duties)
trigger: A customer's data affected in an Education Software incident
deadline: Each customer's own clocks start when it knows; many will treat Education Software's knowledge as theirs
notify: FSA, FTC, students, and state regulators, as each customer decides
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - information for customers; Education Software supplies facts quickly

obligation: Corporate (business associate) notice to Student Health
trigger: Corporate discovers a breach of unsecured Student Health PHI on systems it operates
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (the BAA requires 24 hours)
notify: Student Health Privacy Officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the group SOC is corporate
clock_starts: Discovery by any corporate employee or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: Student Health breach notice to individuals (nonstudent PHI)
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI after the four-factor assessment (164.402)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected nonstudent patient by first-class mail (substitute notice if contact information is insufficient)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 5,800 nonstudent patients in the scenario
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or that would have been known with reasonable diligence, to any workforce member or agent (164.404(a)(2))

obligation: Student Health notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach involving 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (fewer than 500: log and report within 60 days after the end of the calendar year, 164.408(c))
notify: HHS (Secretary), through the breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Student Health media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction affected
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving the state
applies_at_this_tier: Check by state of residence

obligation: Law enforcement delay (HIPAA)
trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede an investigation
deadline: Delay as stated in writing, or up to 30 days if oral and documented
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if law enforcement asks

obligation: Student records at clinics: notice to the owning institutions
citation: Clinic services agreement (college); contract clinic agreements; 34 CFR 99.3 and 99.33 (records are the institutions' FERPA records, not PHI)
trigger: Clinic records of students affected (about 8,100 in the scenario: the college and 2 contracting colleges)
deadline: Contract terms (72 hours standard); Florida third-party agent duty as above
notify: The college's registrar and each contracting college; the institutions decide on student notices under state law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The group determines that a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination; delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination
notify: SEC (public filing to investors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - publicly traded
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. (disclosure committee)
clock_starts: Materiality determination, made without unreasonable delay

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the annual report
notify: Investors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties
notifying_entity: Board risk committee with counsel and the insurer

obligation: Report to law enforcement (voluntary)
citation: Voluntary; OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) treats timely reporting as a mitigating factor
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practicable (runbook target: Day 0 to 1)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but recommended

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). The proposed rule would cover every Title IV institution regardless of size; recheck when final
notifying_entity: n/a (tracked by the Group General Counsel)

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (as soon as practicable; call the carrier before hiring vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered equipment or services identified during performance of a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification, further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Covered article identified during performance of a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification, further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Part 2 record breach
trigger: Breach of substance use disorder program records
deadline: Applies HIPAA breach rules to Part 2 records
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No - no division runs a Part 2 program
